newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 9.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed regional rural banks (RRBs) to invest in corporate shares and debentures and units of mutual funds, the Economic Times reports.

The RBI, however, stipulated that these investments must not exceed five percent of the banks' incremental deposits at the end of the preceding financial year. The central bank also allowed RRBs to buy shares and debentures from the secondary market, the paper says.

** A steep decline in the growth rate of power and mining sector pulled down the overall industrial growth to 9.8 percent during the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) from the level of 12.1 percent during the corresponding period in the last financial year, the Financial Express says.
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.88/90 against the dollar on Thursday compared with the previous close of 35.87/88. The day's range seen at 35.86/91 rupees to a dollar, dealers said.
** Hectic bidding by speculators in blue-chip stocks on increased hopes of positive government announcements helped Indian shares climb to higher levels on Wednesday.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange .BSESN rose 24.76 points, or 0.76 percent to 3,288.88.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index .NSEI gained 17.90 points to 946.70.
** The Delhi index .DE was up 0.07 points at 712.60.
** The Madras index .MDSI fell 33.44 points to 3,152.94.
** The Calcutta index .CALSN lost 1.79 points to 429.43.
